Prune the components of a Random Planted Forest

Source: R/prune.R
prune_components.Rd

Drops the small components of a regression forest's functional decomposition and, optionally, refits one coefficient per kept component. The rule and the threshold are chosen out of bag by default, from the forest itself without refits, or by K-fold cross-validation on the training rows.

Usage

prune_components(
  object,
  data,
  y = NULL,
  ...,
  rule = c("D", "R"),
  tau = c(0, 1e-04, 3e-04, 0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1),
  select = c("1se", "min"),
  select_by = c("oob", "cv"),
  folds = 5L,
  fold_id = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  nthreads = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

object

[rpf]: A fitted regression rpf model.

data

[data.frame | matrix]: The training data of object, in the order of the fit: the predictors as passed to rpf() as x, or the data of the formula or recipe interface. For a formula or recipe fit, data may contain the outcome.

y

[numeric | NULL: NULL]: The outcome of the training rows. Required unless data contains the outcome of a formula or recipe fit.

...

Reserved for future expansion. Unknown arguments are an error.

rule

[character: c("D", "R")]: The rules to consider: "D" drops, "R" drops and refits one coefficient per kept component.

tau

[numeric: c(0, 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1)]: The thresholds to consider, as shares of the variance of the prediction (0.01 = 1%), each at least 0 and below 1.

select

[character(1): "1se"]: How the pair is chosen: "1se" (the largest tau within one standard error of the lowest RMSE) or "min" (the lowest RMSE).

select_by

[character(1): "oob"]: How the candidates are scored, and R's coefficients fitted: "oob" (out of bag, from one purification of object and no refits) or "cv" (K-fold CV with refits of the forest; R's coefficients in sample); see Details.

folds

[integer(1): 5]: The number of folds, used if fold_id is NULL: of the CV, or out of bag of R's refit and of the SE.

fold_id

[vector | NULL: NULL]: The fold of every training row: a vector of length nrow(data) with at least two distinct values. If NULL, the rows are assigned to folds folds at random (after set.seed(seed)).

seed

[integer(1) | NULL: NULL]: The seed set before the random fold assignment and, for the CV, before every fold's refit. If NULL, one is drawn from the current random number stream and stored in the result, so that the choice can be reproduced. The caller's random number state is restored afterwards (see Details).

nthreads

[integer(1) | NULL: NULL]: Number of threads for purifying the forests (object, and the CV's fold fits) and for the fold fits. NULL uses the nthreads object was fitted with. The result does not depend on it.

verbose

[logical(1): FALSE]: Report the progress of the choice.

Value

An object of class rpf_pruned, a list with elements:

  • fit: object (purified).

  • rule, tau: the chosen rule and threshold.

  • intercept: alpha (the forest's intercept f_0 for "D").

  • beta: named vector of the coefficients of the kept components (all 1 for "D"). For "R" with select_by "oob", intercept and beta are fitted on the out-of-bag components (see Details).

  • sets: the predictor sets of the kept components, as column indices.

  • components: a data.frame of every nonzero component of object on the training rows: component (its name, as in predict_components()), order, share, kept, beta (NA if dropped).

  • oob: NULL unless the pair was chosen out of bag; otherwise a data.frame with one row per candidate: rule, tau, oob_rmse (corrected; used for the choice), se_mse (from its per-fold MSEs), oob_rmse_raw and se_mse_raw (uncorrected), n_kept, min and one_se (the two choices). Its attribute n_rows is the number of rows with an OOB family.

  • cv: NULL unless the pair was chosen by CV; otherwise a data.frame with one row per candidate: rule, tau, cv_rmse, se_mse (SE of the CV MSE), n_kept (mean over the folds), min and one_se.

  • select, select_by, fold_id, seed: as used (fold_id and seed are NULL if no choice was made). For a given rule and tau, select_by is "oob" if R's coefficients were fitted out of bag, otherwise NULL.

Use predict() and predict_components() on it, and rpf_marshal() to save it.

Details

The forest is decomposed into its purified components f_S, one per set S of predictors (see purify() and predict_components()), at all orders up to max_interaction, and its intercept f_0. The size of a component is its share of the variance of the prediction f on the training rows, share_S = Var(f_S) / Var(f). The shares are descriptive sizes, not a partition: the components are not orthogonal on the data, so they need not add up to 1. A component is kept if its share is at least tau (and it is not identically zero on the training rows). Two rules are available:

  • "D" (drop): the prediction is f_0 plus the kept components. rule = "D" with tau = 0 is the unpruned forest.

  • "R" (drop and refit): the prediction is alpha + sum(beta_S * f_S) over the kept components, with the intercept alpha and the coefficients beta_S by least squares of y on the kept components (the minimum-norm solution if the components are collinear). The components themselves are not changed, only their scale. With select_by = "oob" (the default, see below), the least squares use each training row's out-of-bag components instead of the forest's own, for a chosen and for a given rule and tau. The forest's own components have fitted the training rows' noise, so least squares on them scale the components up (on California housing the three-way interactions by about 1.3, where new data wants about 0.9). With select_by = "cv", and where the default falls back to it (see below), the least squares use the forest's own components on the training rows.

The choice. If more than one pair of rule and tau is given (the default: both rules and the grid 0, 0.01%, 0.03%, 0.1%, 0.3%, 1%, 3%, 10%), the pair is chosen by its out-of-bag (select_by = "oob", the default) or cross-validated ("cv") RMSE. With select = "1se" (the default), the largest tau whose MSE is within one standard error of the minimum is chosen (the SE is the standard deviation of the per-fold MSEs of the minimum, divided by sqrt(K)), and at that tau the rule with the lower RMSE. With select = "min", the pair with the lowest RMSE is chosen (ties, up to a relative 1e-12: the larger tau, then "D"). "1se" gives sparse models: with "R" fitted out of bag the out-of-bag error changes little over a range of tau, and "min" keeps small components that add nothing on new data.

Out of bag (select_by = "oob"). Every tree family of object is grown on a bootstrap sample of the training rows, and the purification works family by family. So object is purified once more (as purify() does), and on the way every family's components are evaluated at the training rows outside its bootstrap sample. A row's out-of-bag (OOB) component is the mean over its OOB families (about 37% of them), and its OOB intercept likewise. The purification uses the predictors of all training rows, not the outcome, so no outcome information of a row enters its OOB components.

  • The kept components of every tau are those of the final model (the shares of object on the training rows).

  • "D" is scored by the OOB intercept plus the kept OOB components.

  • For "R", alpha and beta_S are fitted as for the final model, by least squares on the OOB components, but only on the rows outside each of K folds (folds, fold_id, seed). They are scored with the OOB components of the fold's rows, so that no row scores coefficients fitted on it. The final model's are fitted on all rows with at least one OOB family.

  • An OOB mean averages m_i families (about 37% of B = ntrees), the final model all B, so the OOB prediction scatters more around its expectation. The OOB MSE is therefore corrected: per row it subtracts (1 / m_i - 1 / B) * v_i, with v_i the across-family variance of the candidate's prediction, estimated from the OOB means over the even and over the odd families (for a row whose OOB families are all even or all odd: the mean estimate of the other rows). Without the correction, the noise of the OOB components makes the candidates look worse than they are. The uncorrected values are reported as oob_rmse_raw.

  • The OOB RMSE is taken over the rows with at least one OOB family, the SE for "1se" from the per-fold MSEs.

  • With few families the OOB means average only one to a few families, and many rows have none (16% at 4 families). In a simulation (p = 6, n = 800, 60 replicates) the corrected OOB error of the unpruned "D" was within 1.5% of the test error at 4, 10, 20 and 50 families, that of "R" within 4.4% except once (+11.5% at 10 families with a 3-way interaction), and the OOB choice was as good as the CV's or better from 10 families on (within 0.4% in test error, or better by 7-10% where the CV's fold fits choose poorly). Below 10 families (ntrees), the default select_by scores by CV instead (with a message); an explicit select_by = "oob" warns.

  • A deterministic forest has no out-of-bag rows, and a forest restored by rpf_unmarshal() from a blob made by an earlier version has no in-bag counts (with a message): with the default select_by, they are scored by CV instead.

  • A given rule "R" and tau (no choice) is fitted on the OOB components too, with the same fallbacks: below 10 families or without in-bag counts its coefficients are fitted in sample (with a message), and so they are for a deterministic forest. A given "D" needs no OOB components.

  • Factor predictors are coded by the outcome of all training rows: their levels are ordered by the mean outcome (regression), by the share of the second class (binary classification) or by the first principal component of the class proportions (three or more classes; Coppersmith, Hong and Hosking 1999). So a row's own outcome enters the coding its OOB families split on: with factors the OOB error is somewhat optimistic.

Cross-validation (select_by = "cv"). For each fold, the forest is refitted with the parameters of object on the other folds (after set.seed(seed), the same for every fold), its components, shares and refit are computed on those rows, and every candidate is scored on the held-out fold. The CV RMSE is sqrt(sum(SSE_k) / n), summing the squared errors over the K folds.

The chosen (or given) pair is then applied to object itself (not refitted): its components and shares on data, and for "R" the least squares on the OOB components of data's rows (out of bag) or on its components on data (by CV). data and y must therefore be the rows object was trained on, in the order of the fit (checked).

Purification. object is purified in place at all orders, as purify() does, if it is not purified yet. This does not change its predictions. A forest purified with a maxp_interaction below its order is purified again at all orders, with a message: the pruning needs every component. The out-of-bag path purifies object (again) in mode 2, which gives the same components (a mode-1 purification's up to rounding).

Random numbers. The folds are drawn after set.seed(seed), and the CV's fold fits after it too. Afterwards the random number stream is restored to its state on entry (after drawing seed if it is NULL), so the call does not reset the caller's stream.

Cost. The out-of-bag choice purifies object once and evaluates each family's components at its OOB rows; it needs no fit. The CV fits and purifies the forest K more times. Both evaluate the components on the training rows: only those the purified forest stores (at most sum(choose(p, seq_len(max_interaction))), usually far fewer: the subsets of the trees' predictor sets), in one pass over the rows. The memory is about n doubles per stored component, a few times that for the out-of-bag choice. nthreads speeds up the fits and the purification.

Only regression forests are supported.

See also

predict.rpf_pruned(), predict_components(), purify().

Examples

# A main effect and a pure interaction
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(runif(600 * 4, -1, 1), ncol = 4, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("x", 1:4)))
y <- x[, 1] + 2 * x[, 2] * x[, 3] + rnorm(600, sd = 0.3)
fit <- rpf(x, y, max_interaction = 2, ntrees = 20, splits = 50)

# Rule and threshold chosen out of bag (no refits): the largest tau within one SE
# of the lowest error
pruned <- prune_components(fit, x, y, seed = 1)
pruned
#> ── Pruned Random Planted Forest ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Rule R (drop + refit one coefficient per component, fitted out of bag), tau = 10% of Var(prediction)
#> Chosen by out-of-bag error (1-SE rule; R refitted in 5 folds, seed 1) among 16 candidates.
#> 
#> Nonzero components: 9
#> Kept:    2 (by order 1: 1, 2: 1)
#> Dropped: 7 (by order 1: 3, 2: 4)
#> Largest dropped: x1:x3 (share 1.8%); dropped shares sum to 4.4%
#> 
#> Intercept: -0.0162521
#> Kept components (largest first), share on the training rows and coefficient:
#>  component share beta 
#>  x1        61%   0.977
#>  x2:x3     19%   1.863
pruned$oob
#>    rule   tau  oob_rmse     se_mse oob_rmse_raw se_mse_raw n_kept   min one_se
#> 1     D 0e+00 0.5361833 0.01395762    0.5638097 0.01187499      9 FALSE  FALSE
#> 2     D 1e-04 0.5361833 0.01395762    0.5638097 0.01187499      9 FALSE  FALSE

#> 4     D 1e-03 0.5333645 0.01401006    0.5607863 0.01162696      7 FALSE  FALSE
#> 5     D 3e-03 0.5204500 0.01389558    0.5467446 0.01264863      5 FALSE  FALSE
#> 6     D 1e-02 0.5201940 0.01503833    0.5452333 0.01395539      4 FALSE  FALSE
#> 7     D 3e-02 0.5044697 0.02196168    0.5187196 0.02147003      2 FALSE  FALSE
#> 8     D 1e-01 0.5044697 0.02196168    0.5187196 0.02147003      2 FALSE  FALSE
#> 9     R 0e+00 0.3836019 0.02250883    0.4397841 0.02277146      9 FALSE  FALSE
#> 10    R 1e-04 0.3836019 0.02250883    0.4397841 0.02277146      9 FALSE  FALSE
#> 11    R 3e-04 0.3836019 0.02250883    0.4397841 0.02277146      9 FALSE  FALSE

#> 16    R 1e-01 0.3800078 0.01757644    0.4315554 0.01610271      2  TRUE   TRUE

# ... or the lowest error
prune_components(fit, x, y, select = "min", seed = 1)
#> ── Pruned Random Planted Forest ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Rule R (drop + refit one coefficient per component, fitted out of bag), tau = 10% of Var(prediction)
#> Chosen by out-of-bag error (lowest OOB RMSE; R refitted in 5 folds, seed 1) among 16 candidates.

# ... or by 5-fold CV
pruned_cv <- prune_components(fit, x, y, select_by = "cv", seed = 1)
pruned_cv$cv

prune_components(fit, x, y, rule = "R", tau = 0.01)
